reading.body:
Amazon Web Services recorded $717 billion in revenue in 2025 while operating two major AI product lines: SageMaker for full-stack ML lifecycle management and Bedrock for managed foundation model access.

AWS sits at the intersection of compute supply and AI demand. SageMaker's architecture—unified data lakes, model monitoring, bias detection, and governance tools—reflects the infrastructure required to run production AI at scale. Bedrock's API model with VPC support and IAM integration suggests AWS is positioning itself as the managed layer between foundation models and enterprise users who want isolation and control. Both products point to a company treating AI not as a feature but as a platform business spanning data, compute, and model serving.

The scale here matters for power and buildings. A $717 billion revenue company in cloud services operates data centers globally to deliver these products. The fact that SageMaker includes toxicity detection, guardrails, and data lineage tracking indicates AWS is building compliance and observability into the compute layer itself. This is not decorative. As regulatory exposure grows, the infrastructure provider that bakes governance into the platform gains advantage over those that bolt it on later.

The data does not specify AWS's capital spending, energy consumption, or data center locations. It does not break out AI revenue from total AWS revenue or show whether SageMaker and Bedrock are growing faster than legacy services. It does not name which foundation models Bedrock serves or how much compute AWS allocates to these two products versus others.

profile_text.body:
Amazon Web Services is a division of Amazon that provides cloud computing and AI infrastructure. Per its website, Amazon SageMaker is positioned as "the center for all your data, analytics, and AI," offering an integrated development environment for machine learning and analytics workloads. The company describes SageMaker Unified Studio as bringing together AWS ML and analytics capabilities in a single interface, with unified access to data across data lakes, data warehouses, and third-party sources.

SageMaker's AI capabilities span the full machine learning lifecycle, including model training, customization, and deployment on distributed infrastructure. The platform includes purpose-built tools for IDEs, distributed training, inference, AI operations, governance, and observability. AWS also offers Amazon Bedrock, a managed foundation model API service featuring IAM integration, VPC support, model evaluation tools, and AgentCore for agent orchestration. Both products incorporate generative AI capabilities, with Amazon Q Developer available to assist with model development, data discovery, and SQL query generation through natural language interfaces.

AWS is a public company headquartered in Seattle, WA, with 2024 revenue of $716,924,000,000 (ticker: AMZN, CIK: 0001018724). The held facts indicate AWS has litigation exposure in Washington state, with 96 cases tracked in that jurisdiction. AWS does not currently maintain an MCP server listing.
